chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mihrān narrated from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who says that he will offer such-and-such as a gift to the Kaʿbah; what is required of him if he is unable to provide what he intended to offer?

He عليه السلام said: “If he made it a nadhr and does not own it, then there is nothing upon him. But if it is something he owns, such as a غلام, a جارية, or something similar, he should sell it and buy perfume with its price, then perfume the Kaʿbah with it. And if it is an animal, then there is nothing upon him.”

key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: the Kaʿbah, the sacred House in Makkah
key_terms.جَارِيَةً: a female slave owned as property in the legal context of the text
key_terms.غُلَامًا: a male slave owned as property in the legal context of the text
key_terms.نَذْرًا: a vow binding oneself to an act or offering
key_terms.يُهْدِي: to offer or dedicate as a gift

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone vows to dedicate something to the Kaʿbah but cannot fulfill it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about a nadhr connected to gifting something to the Kaʿbah when the person cannot fulfill it as stated. If the vowed item is not owned, nothing is due; if it is owned and of a transferable kind, it is sold and its value used for perfume for the Kaʿbah, while no obligation is established regarding an animal in this case.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4315 - Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Mihran narrated from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as), who said:
I asked him about a man who says that he will offer such-and-such as a gift to the Ka'bah, but he is unable to fulfill it.

Imam (as) said: "If he made it a vow and does not own it, then there is nothing upon him. However, if it is something he owns, such as a slave, a maid, or something similar, he should sell it and use the proceeds to buy perfume, which he will use to anoint the Ka'bah. But if it is an animal, then there is nothing required of him."
